notes.1: Most candidates answered this relatively straightforward question correctly, choosing C . This question relates to the provision of information by the accountant to management.
notes.2: This question asked candidates to apply the accounting equation, which is a basic yet fundamental topic on the syllabus. This question appears at the start of the question paper and therefore is relatively straightforward, and most candidates answered correctly. The correct answer is B .
notes.3: This question required candidates to identify that a loss for the year would be credited to the income statement and debited to the capital account. The correct answer was C . Some candidates found this question challenging and selected an incorrect option.
notes.6: Question 6 required candidates to identify which of the items listed would be shown on a statement of account. The correct answer is B . While many candidates answered correctly, some thought that trade discount would be shown on a statement of account.
notes.12: Candidates were required to calculate the balance on the bank statement. The bank statement balance should be ($449 + $175 – $424 =) $200. However, the bank has incorrectly charged $10 interest, so the actual bank statement balance is $190. The correct answer was A .
notes.16: Question 16 required candidates to identify the correct statement about depreciation. The correct answer was D . While many candidates identified the correct statement, some candidates did not notice that option C related to current assets and so they selected that option instead.
notes.19: This question required candidates to calculate the inventory valuation for two types of inventory. The t-shirts were valued at 100 × $15 = $1500. The dresses were valued at 200 × $30 = $6000. The total inventory valuation is therefore $7500. The correct answer is A . While many candidates identified the correct valuation, some candidates selected an option based on the overall totals for cost and for net realisable value, rather than on the cost and net realisable value for each type of inventory.
notes.20: This question asks candidates to identify which error would result in gross profit being overstated. If opening inventory is omitted from the income statement, then cost of sales is understated. Therefore, gross profit is overstated. The correct answer is B . Some candidates seemed to find this question slightly challenging.
notes.26: Candidates were required to calculate the percentage dividend which shareholders would receive. The profit to be paid as dividend was ($13 000 – $6000 – $3000 =) $4 000. $4 000 / $50 000 × 100 = 8% The correct answer is A .
notes.28: This question covered the topic of clubs and societies. Candidates were asked to identify what is included in an income and expenditure account. The correct answer is D . Amounts received and paid during the year are shown in the receipts and payments account, and not in the income and expenditure account.
notes.31: This question covered the topic of incomplete records. Candidates were required to calculate the net profit. Although many candidates chose the correct option, some candidates found this challenging. Total sales are $36 000 × 100/90 = $40 000. The net profit is 30% of $40 000 which is $12 000. The correct answer is D .
notes.32: This question covered the topic of interpretation of accounting ratios. Candidates were asked to identify which business controls its overheads most efficiently. Expenses incurred are 18% (i.e., 30% – 12%) of the revenue of the business. This is the lowest of the four options. The correct answer is D .
